sub_graphs.title: Discovery v5: Session Establishment Handshake
sub_graphs.description: Models the session establishment handshake protocol between two nodes, from initial message through WHOAREYOU challenge to authenticated session

nodes.label: No Active Session
nodes.description: No cryptographic session exists between the two nodes; outgoing messages cannot be encrypted

nodes.label: Send Ordinary Message Packet
nodes.description: Send a message packet (flag=0) with a random nonce; if no session exists, the recipient cannot decrypt it

nodes.label: WHOAREYOU Challenge Received
nodes.description: Recipient could not decrypt the message and responded with a WHOAREYOU packet containing id-nonce and ENR sequence number

nodes.label: Compute Handshake Session Keys
nodes.description: Generate ephemeral key pair, perform ECDH with recipient's public key, derive session keys via HKDF, and create id-signature proving node identity

nodes.label: Send Handshake Message Packet
nodes.description: Send a handshake packet (flag=2) containing ephemeral public key, id-signature, optional ENR record, and the encrypted original message

nodes.label: Verify Handshake and Establish Session
nodes.description: Recipient verifies id-signature, derives same session keys from ECDH, and decrypts the message to establish the bidirectional session

nodes.label: Session Established
nodes.description: Both nodes share session encryption keys; subsequent messages use ordinary message packets with AES-GCM encryption

edges.label: Attempt to communicate with peer
Peer cannot decrypt, sends WHOAREYOU challenge
Generate ephemeral keys and derive session secrets
Send authenticated handshake with encrypted message
Recipient processes handshake packet
Handshake verified, session keys derived on both sides

sub_graphs.title: Discovery v5: Node Lookup and Routing Table
sub_graphs.description: Models the Kademlia-based node lookup process and routing table maintenance

nodes.label: Node Lookup Initiated
nodes.description: A lookup for the k closest nodes to a target ID has been initiated

nodes.label: Select Alpha Closest Known Nodes
nodes.description: Select alpha (typically 3) closest nodes to the target from the local routing table as initial query targets

nodes.label: Send FINDNODE Request
nodes.description: Send FINDNODE message to selected peers specifying logarithmic distances from the target; recommended limit is 16 result nodes

nodes.label: NODES Response Received
nodes.description: Received NODES response containing ENR records of nodes at the requested distances

nodes.label: Update Routing Table with Discovered Nodes
nodes.description: Add newly discovered nodes to the appropriate k-bucket (max 16 entries per bucket); if bucket full, check liveness of least-recently-seen node

nodes.label: Evict Stale Node from K-Bucket
nodes.description: If least-recently-seen node does not respond to PING, remove it and add the new node

nodes.label: Lookup Complete
nodes.description: The k closest nodes to the target have been queried and responded; lookup terminates

edges.label: Begin lookup by selecting initial peers
Query selected peers
Peer responds with NODES message containing ENR records
Integrate discovered nodes
K-bucket full, evict stale entry if necessary
All k closest nodes queried and responded

external_entities.name: Remote Discovery Node
external_entities.description: Another node in the discovery network that responds to FINDNODE queries with NODES responses

sub_graphs.title: Discovery v5: Packet Encryption and Authentication
sub_graphs.description: Models the security mechanisms protecting discv5 packets including header masking, AES-GCM encryption, and nonce management

nodes.label: Outgoing Message Ready for Encoding
nodes.description: A protocol message (PING, FINDNODE, etc.) is ready to be encoded into a wire packet

nodes.label: Generate Unique 96-bit Nonce
nodes.description: Generate a unique nonce: encode outgoing message count into first 32 bits, fill remaining 64 bits with random data to prevent reuse

nodes.label: Encrypt Message with AES-GCM
nodes.description: Encrypt the message payload using AES-128-GCM with the session key, nonce, and additional authenticated data (masking IV + header)

nodes.label: Mask Header with AES-CTR
nodes.description: Encrypt the static header using AES-128-CTR with the destination node ID as key and a random 16-byte masking IV

nodes.label: Packet Ready to Send
nodes.description: Complete packet assembled: masking IV + masked header + encrypted message, max 1280 bytes

nodes.label: Incoming Packet Received
nodes.description: A raw UDP packet has been received from the network

nodes.label: Unmask Header
nodes.description: Decrypt the header using local node ID as AES-CTR key to reveal protocol-id, version, flag, nonce, and authdata

nodes.label: Verify Protocol ID and Version
nodes.description: Check protocol-id is 'discv5' and version is supported; reject packet otherwise

nodes.label: Decrypt and Authenticate Message
nodes.description: Decrypt message using AES-GCM with session key; if decryption fails (no session or wrong key), send WHOAREYOU

nodes.label: Message Authenticated and Decrypted
nodes.description: Message integrity verified via GCM tag; content available for processing

edges.label: Begin packet encoding
Encrypt message with unique nonce
Mask header to prevent identification
Packet fully assembled
Raw UDP packet arrives from network
Decrypt header using local node ID
Check protocol identifier
Attempt message decryption with session key
GCM tag verified, message authentic

external_entities.name: UDP Network
external_entities.description: The underlying UDP transport carrying discv5 packets; unreliable, unordered, and potentially adversarial

ambiguities.text: The specification recommends timeout values of '500ms for a single request/response and 1s for the handshake' but does not mandate them, leaving implementations to choose potentially inconsistent values.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the recommended values are used as defaults. Implementations may tune but should not deviate significantly to maintain interoperability.

ambiguities.text: The topic advertisement system (REGTOPIC, TICKET, REGCONFIRMATION, TOPICQUERY) is described but marked as 'not finalized' with implementations advised against support.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Exclude topic advertisement from the runtime behavior model as it is not yet part of the stable protocol.

ambiguities.text: The specification states implementations 'should not re-send packets if the recipient doesn't respond' treating UDP as lossy, but higher-level lookup algorithms imply retries by querying additional nodes.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume no packet-level retransmission; reliability is achieved at the lookup algorithm level by querying multiple nodes.

implicit_assumptions.description: It is assumed that an attacker cannot observe the mapping between node IDs and IP addresses for nodes they have not directly communicated with, due to header masking.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Traffic analysis could enable targeted eclipse attacks by identifying and blocking specific nodes based on their network activity patterns.

implicit_assumptions.description: UDP packets are assumed to generally arrive within the timeout period (500ms) over typical internet paths.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: High-latency or lossy network conditions could cause excessive WHOAREYOU challenges, degrading discovery performance and potentially enabling DoS amplification.

implicit_assumptions.description: ENR records are assumed to be self-authenticated via their signature, preventing forgery of node identity information.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Forged ENR records could redirect discovery queries to attacker-controlled nodes, enabling eclipse attacks or network partitioning.
